episode_title: He Lost His Flag in 1877 and Waited 35 Years: General Nogi Maresuke
youtube_title: He Lost His Emperor's Flag at 27 — and Carried It for 35 Years | General Nogi of Port Arthur
youtube_description:
In February 1877 a 27-year-old officer lost the flag his emperor had given his regiment, asked to be punished, and was left to go on living. Thirty-five years later, after Port Arthur and the deaths of both his sons, his last testament named that flag in its very first article. If you had been his commander in 1877, would you have punished him, or told him to live?

📰 Your reporter: Tokio Kamiya, a former Tokyo foreign correspondent. His grandfather's brass pocket watch carries him to one day of Japan's past at a time. He can watch and he can speak, but he can never change what happens. This time he files his dispatch from a road north of Kumamoto Castle on the evening of 22 February 1877, during the Satsuma Rebellion.

scenes.narration: First, the flag is a gift. Each regiment receives its colours from the emperor himself, in a ceremony, in his name. Second, to these men it is more than cloth. scenes.narration: A young private sits against a farmhouse wall, binding his own arm. He takes me for a travelling merchant. I ask him what happened. The flag, he says, and stops. The bearer was a young lieutenant, he tells me, cut down in the confusion, and in the dark the Satsuma men carried the colours away. He looks back down the road. The major, he says, looked like a man who wanted to walk back into the dark. I write it down. I do not know how much of it he saw himself.
